title: Fever: home care and when to worry
content: For a mild fever, rest, drink plenty of fluids and avoid heavy clothing. Paracetamol may be used according to the label when a doctor is unavailable, but never give aspirin to a child. See a doctor if a fever lasts more than 3 days, is very high, or comes with a stiff neck, confusion, a rash, or trouble breathing.

title: Cough and cold relief
content: Rest, drink warm fluids and use honey with lemon for a sore throat (not for infants). Saline nasal drops help a blocked nose. A cough usually clears in 2-3 weeks. See a doctor if you cough up blood, have high fever, chest pain, or breathlessness, or the cough lasts beyond 3 weeks.

title: Headache and migraine basics
content: Rest in a quiet, dark room, stay hydrated and avoid skipping meals. Regular sleep helps many headaches. Seek urgent care for the worst headache of your life, a headache with fever and a stiff neck, sudden weakness, vision changes, or one that follows a head injury.

title: Stomach / abdominal pain guidance
content: For mild stomach pain, rest, eat light meals and stay hydrated. Seek urgent care for severe or worsening pain, pain in the lower right abdomen, blood in stools or vomit, high fever, or vomiting that will not stop.

title: Chest discomfort: an important warning
content: Chest pain or pressure, especially with sweating, nausea, shortness of breath, or pain spreading to the arm, neck or jaw, can be a heart emergency. Call your local emergency number or go to the nearest hospital immediately. Do not wait for online advice.

title: Breathing difficulty
content: Difficulty breathing, wheezing, or a blue tinge to the lips is an emergency. Sit upright, stay calm, and seek urgent care immediately. Do not wait for an online consultation.

title: Diarrhoea and dehydration
content: Prevent dehydration by drinking an oral rehydration solution or frequent small sips of water. Eat bland, easy-to-digest food. See a doctor for bloody stools, high fever, severe pain, or signs of dehydration such as a dry mouth, little urine, or dizziness.

title: Constipation relief
content: Drink more water, eat fibre-rich foods (fruits, vegetables, whole grains) and stay active. Regular toilet habits help. See a doctor if it lasts more than 2-3 weeks, stool has blood, or it is painful and recurring.

title: Acid reflux and heartburn
content: Eat smaller meals, avoid lying down right after eating, and limit spicy, fried or acidic foods. See a doctor if symptoms happen often, cause trouble swallowing, weight loss, or wake you at night regularly.

title: Skin rash and itching
content: For most rashes, keep the skin clean, dry and moisturised. Cool compresses ease itching; avoid scratching. Seek urgent care for a rash that appears suddenly with fever, a purple rash that does not fade when pressed, swelling of the lips or face, or trouble breathing.

title: Joint, muscle and back pain
content: For mild sprains and strains, rest, apply ice for the first 48 hours, then gentle heat, and keep the area moving within comfort. See a doctor for pain that follows a serious injury, lasts beyond 2 weeks, comes with numbness or weakness, or stops you from standing or walking.

title: Cuts, burns and minor injury
content: Rinse a clean cut under running water, apply pressure with a clean cloth to stop bleeding, then cover with a sterile dressing. Cool a minor burn under cold running water for 10-20 minutes. Seek urgent care for deep, gaping or heavily bleeding wounds, burns larger than your palm, burns to the face or hands, or signs of infection (heat, pus, red streaks).

title: High blood pressure basics
content: If you have high blood pressure, reduce salt, keep physically active, maintain a healthy weight, limit alcohol and take medicines exactly as prescribed. Do not stop medication on your own. Seek urgent care for a very high reading with headache, chest pain, blurred vision or shortness of breath.

title: Diabetes self-care
content: Keep regular meals, monitor your sugar as advised by your doctor, and take medication on time. For a low-sugar episode, take fast-acting sugar (glucose, juice) immediately. Seek urgent care for very high sugar with vomiting, breathlessness, or drowsiness.

title: Anxiety, stress and sleep
content: Try regular breathing exercises, a fixed sleep schedule, limited caffeine, and daily movement. Talk to a doctor or counsellor if anxiety, low mood or poor sleep affects your daily life for more than two weeks. If you ever have thoughts of harming yourself, tell someone and seek help immediately.

title: Urinary symptoms and UTI
content: Drink plenty of water and keep the bladder area clean for mild irritation. See a doctor for burning or painful urination, blood in urine, fever with back pain, or urinary symptoms that do not improve in a day or two.

title: Eye discomfort and vision
content: Rest your eyes and blink often if they feel strained. For mild redness or foreign body, rinse with clean water. Seek urgent care for sudden vision loss, severe eye pain, trauma, or a sudden change in vision.

title: Ear, nose and throat care
content: For mild cold-related ear or sinus pressure, rest, hydrate and use a warm compress. See a doctor for severe ear pain, ear discharge, sudden hearing loss, a persistent sore throat with high fever, or difficulty swallowing.

title: Fever and illness in children
content: A child with a fever should rest and drink fluids. Never give aspirin to a child. Seek immediate care for a baby under 3 months with any fever, a fever with a rash, lethargy, poor feeding, a stiff neck, or a seizure.

title: Advice during pregnancy
content: Attend all antenatal check-ups and follow your doctor's advice on nutrition and supplements. Seek urgent care for vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, severe headache or visual changes, reduced baby movements, or leaking of fluid.

title: Medication safety rules
content: Take medicines exactly as prescribed and never change or stop doses on your own. Do not share prescriptions. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about interactions before combining medicines, and check that a medicine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. If you suspect an overdose, seek emergency care immediately.

title: Tooth and gum pain
content: Rinse with warm salt water, avoid very hot or very sweet foods, and see a dentist for a toothache that persists beyond a day or two. Seek urgent care for facial swelling, swelling that affects breathing, or severe pain.

title: Preventing dehydration
content: Drink water regularly throughout the day, more in heat or with activity. Watch for a dry mouth, dark urine, dizziness or fatigue as early signs of dehydration. Seek urgent care for confusion, fainting, or an inability to keep fluids down.

title: Balanced nutrition basics
content: A balanced plate has vegetables, fruit, whole grains, protein and healthy fats, with water as the main drink. Skip fad diets. For unexplained or rapid weight loss or gain, see a doctor.

title: Common concerns for older adults
content: Prevent falls at home by clearing clutter, good lighting, and using support where needed. Report any new dizziness, confusion, or memory changes to a doctor. Seek urgent care after any fall with a head bump, new confusion, or inability to move a limb.

title: Allergy reactions
content: Avoid known triggers, keep a record of what causes reactions, and follow your doctor's allergy plan. Anaphylaxis (swelling of lips or throat, trouble breathing, dizziness) is an emergency — call emergency services immediately.

title: Before your doctor visit
content: Bring a list of your symptoms (when they started, how they change), all medicines you take, and any questions. On the SmartCare platform you can book a verified doctor, join a video consult, see your prescription and symptom timeline, and pay your consultation fee online.

title: General rule for seeing a doctor
content: See a doctor for symptoms that are severe, getting worse, lasting more than 2-3 weeks, or affecting your daily life. Seek emergency care immediately for chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe bleeding, unconsciousness, or signs of a stroke.
